audit.whatIsWrong: Three slots — breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t — tell the Galio player that 'your Hookshot is disabled inside it'. Galio has no Hookshot; that is Camille's E. And the single most actionable interaction in the matchup is never stated.
audit.why: Galio's dash is Justice Punch. Miasma does ground it — Riot's text is explicit: 'slowing, grounding, and lightly damaging enemies that pass through them. Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities.' Separately, Petrifying Gaze 'stuns any enemies in front of her that are facing her and slows any others with their back turned' — so turning away downgrades her ultimate from a stun to a slow. Nothing on the page says that.
audit.corrected: Hookshot replaced with Justice Punch throughout, and the face-the-gaze rule written into the key-interactions slot, the loading tip, the 2+ items stage and the late text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Skill on all seven stages, but content whys[1] through whys[5] say she owns the trade tempo, beats your combo and keeps 'the poke war firmly hers'. whys[6] is worse: it sits in the 2+ items slot and opens 'Level 6 is the verdict'. The full layer also calls Cassiopeia 'him' throughout and credits Galio with a 'passive shield'.
audit.why: An all-Skill chart with prose that hands her five stages is a page arguing with itself. The 2+ items row needs to be about 2+ items, not level 6.
audit.corrected: Chart left alone — Skill is defensible for a lane where her damage is 100% magic and your W is built for it. The whys rewritten so each stage explains the actual edge and lands where the chart lands; whys[6] moved onto the 2+ items window; pronouns and the passive-shield claim fixed.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why ends with the boilerplate 'Reassess his ultimate too', phases[5].why claims Stormsurge/Riftmaker is your spike with no reference to hers, and no cooldown number appears anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Miasma is 24s at rank 1 — by far the longest cooldown in the lane and the entire engage window. Noxious Blast is 3.5s flat and Twin Fang 0.75s, which is why a poke war is unwinnable and a baited-Miasma window is everything.
audit.corrected: 24s / 3.5s / 0.75s written into the stage lines, the cooldown block and the all-in windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appears nowhere despite Twin Fang healing on every cast into a poisoned target.
audit.why: Twin Fang 'heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt' on a 0.75s cooldown. In a long lane that is the sustain that undoes your chip, and Oblivion Orb is the answer.
audit.corrected: Oblivion Orb added to itemization, the loading tip, the 2+ items why and the late text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer calls Serpentine Grace 'the no-boots move-speed passive'.
audit.why: Riot's description is only 'All Move Speed bonuses are more effective on Cassiopeia' — nothing about boots. I could not verify the boots restriction from any local file, so I removed the claim rather than repeat it.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as Serpentine Grace amplifying her move-speed buffs.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash: you have only Winds of War with no engage, and she only has Noxious Blast, so just contest last-hits, dodge the poison clouds, and bank mana for level 3. The first danger window is 2-3 as her poison ramp comes online — she stacks Noxious Blast and chunks you with Twin Fang from outside your Justice Punch range, and a Miasma grounds the dash so you can't punish. The answer is your identity button: channel Shield of Durand into her Twin Fang to gut the magic damage, then look to release the taunt and E in. Don't chase blind into a cloud, but this is a Galio-favoured lane precisely because your W eats exactly the damage she deals.

The first danger window is 2-3 as her poison ramp comes online — she stacks Noxious Blast and chunks you with Twin Fang on a 0.75s cooldown from outside Justice Punch range, healing off every cast, and a Miasma grounds the dash so you can't punish. The answer is your identity button: channel Shield of Durand into her Twin Fang to gut the magic damage, then release the taunt and E in. Miasma is 24s at rank 1, so the moment she spends it the level is yours.

edits.before: This is her best stretch, but you don't have to lose it — you have to bait the Miasma. Her poison plus the no-boots move-speed passive lets her kite your Justice Punch, and a well-placed Miasma grounds the dash outright, so every clean all-in starts by making her burn the grounding. The lane-defining tool is level 6: Hero's Entrance means you don't out-poke her at all, you R to mid or bot, taunt their carry, and convert a hard lane into a map lead while she's stuck farming. When she does step forward, facetank a committed poison burst behind Shield of Durand's amplified magic reduction, release the taunt, and E-knockup into her — her Petrifying Gaze is a face-stun, so she can't peel that the way she kites your dash.
edits.after: This is her best stretch, but you don't have to lose it — you have to bait the Miasma. Her poison plus Serpentine Grace, which amplifies every move-speed buff she picks up, lets her kite your Justice Punch, and a well-placed Miasma grounds the dash outright, so every clean all-in starts by making her burn the cloud. The lane-defining tool is level 6: Hero's Entrance means you don't out-poke her at all, you R to mid or bot, taunt their carry, and convert a hard lane into a map lead while she's stuck farming. When she does step forward, facetank a committed poison burst behind Shield of Durand's amplified magic reduction, release the taunt, and E-knockup into her. And if Petrifying Gaze comes out, turn away — facing her is the stun, backs turned is only a slow.

edits.before: Let it run long in a 1v1 and she takes over: at 2+ items her sustained poison out-DPSes your tank-AP trades and Miasma permanently zones your Justice Punch, so the straight side-lane duel slips away. But your value was never the solo duel — it's R-presence and the taunt. In teamfights you flash-taunt her off her kite line and your team deletes her before her poison ramps, and Hero's Entrance keeps her honest across the map. Don't try to solo her in a side lane late; group, soak her poison behind Shield of Durand, and force her to commit Petrifying Gaze where your team can collapse, since a face-stun she's forced to use defensively wins her nothing.

Buy Oblivion Orb before that window, not after. But your value was never the solo duel — it's R-presence and the taunt. In teamfights you flash-taunt her off her kite line and your team deletes her before the poison ramps. Don't try to solo her in a side lane late; group, soak her poison behind Shield of Durand, and turn your back the instant Petrifying Gaze fires so it lands as a slow instead of a stun.
